entities.summary: Rainerius (c. 1115/1117 – 1160) was a 12th-century Italian Benedictine monk, abbot, and cardinal who played a crucial role in shaping the spiritual landscape of the medieval Mediterranean. Born in Italy, Rainerius spent most of his life in the Holy Roman Empire, where he worked tirelessly to promote monastic reform and defend the rights of the Church. His dedication to his faith and his people earned him recognition from the papacy, leading to his appointment as cardinal-deacon of Sutri. Rainerius's legacy extends beyond his own time, as his writings and teachings continue to inspire spiritual seekers to this day. According to historical records, Rainerius was canonized as a saint by the Catholic Church in 1161, solidifying his place as a revered figure in Christian history. His feast day, June 17, remains a celebrated observance in many parts of the world, symbolizing the enduring power of faith and devotion.
